This Widebody Chevy Camaro Has a Biblical Mod, What’s Your Take on the Message?
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | rohanawheels
Even though we are perfectly capable of writing a story about the Chevrolet Camaro without reminding ourselves that this model is dead and buried, we refuse to do that. Well, at least until General Motors brings back this iconic nameplate.
That might happen in late 2028, probably for the 2029 model year, as the moniker is indeed coming back from the dead. However, instead of launching it as a two-door coupe, perhaps joined by a two-door convertible body style, it appears that the bowtie brand has settled for something else instead: a four-door sedan.
Word on the street is that the next-generation Chevrolet Camaro might only be offered as a sedan, so it will inevitably take on the four-door version of the modern-day Dodge Charger. For what it’s worth, it will likely annihilate it, at least from an enthusiast’s perspective, because it will launch with V8 firepower, and probably a stick shift channeling the yet-unknown output and thrust to the rear wheels.
But the new-age Dodge Charger is also getting a V8 engine for the first time ever, so it will finally be able to take a proper swing at the S650 Ford Mustang. The latter is the only muscle car in production to be offered with a V8. And given that the new Chevy Camaro will launch as a four-door, and that the latest Charger is also offered in this body style, it is possible that the Dearborn company might eventually consider launching a Mustang Sedan.
Photo: Instagram | rohanawheels Now, that’s a story for another time (actually, it’s been discussed many times), so instead, we should get back on track and start writing about the pictured Chevrolet Camaro , which looks extremely muscular due to its aftermarket makeover. The first thing that stands out is the widebody design, highlighted by the wider wheel arches at the front and the extremely broad shoulders, joined by a new hood that is also on the muscular side of things.
Moreover, there is also a new apron attached to the front bumper, and by the looks of it, it is adjustable. The side skirt attachments are also new, and at the rear, it seems to sport new taillights. The rear bumper is new, and so is the diffuser, and this component is on the very large side of things. Not only that, but it also features cutouts in the middle for the four exhaust tips. The trunk lid is decorated with a large wing, and there are also attachments on the rear windscreen, and the rear three-quarter windows.
Rohana shared pictures of this modded Chevrolet Camaro on its social media channels earlier this week for a very simple reason: it rides on one of their wheel sets. The alloys are called the Rohana Forged RFG29. This model is available in unibloc and trinity options, with hidden, fully exposed, or 50/50 hardware, and can be specified with carbon fiber options, and ordered in several premium and custom finishes.
Photo: Instagram | rohanawheels The sizes available range from 18 to 24 inches, and the widths from 8.5 to 13 inches, respectively, and the starting price of the full set in the smallest offering available is $6,000. That’s before factoring in other options, and before buying the tires, obviously. In this case, the Y-spoke wheels feature a black look, have the Rohana logo on the 3D center caps, and they spin around the red brake calipers that sport Brembo branding in white on them.
The brake calipers are the things that provide the most contrast to this Chevy Camaro’s exterior, as the muscle car in question is presented in black. Now, about that Biblical reference made in the title, it is all about the new trim on the front fenders. These read “Psalm 23:4,” and that says “Even though I walk through the darkest valley (the valley of the shadow of death), I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.” And that’s definitely a very strong message.
The interior of this muscle car, which also features a Rohana decal on the front windscreen, is only partially visible through the windows in the images shared online by the wheelmaker recently. Still, we can see that the seats are shown in red, and that’s likely leather upholstery, and the pillars and headliner are black. We reckon a bit more red could also be on deck on the inside, but that’s our two cents, and should be taken accordingly.
Now, this is a very impressive-looking Chevrolet Camaro that definitely deserves its 15 minutes of online fame, hence why decided to share it with you. But I promise we can still be friends even if you do not dig the way this tuned muscle car looks. So, what’s your take on it? Is the tuning job a yay or a nay in your book? Oregon utility Pacific General Electric (“PGE”) is highlighting the environmental, health, and grid benefits to electrifying medium- and heavy-duty commercial trucks, calling the battery-backed big rigs “batteries on wheels.”
Earlier this month, Oregon hosted its first, fleet-focused electric ride-and-drive event, bringing everything from Class 8 electric semi trucks and medium-duty “last mile” delivery trucks to battery-powered equipment assets like wheel loaders and excavators together in one place so the state’s fleet operators (and fleet buyers) could experience the latest generation of commercial EVs for themselves.
More importantly, Portland utility PGE was also on-hand, along with local NBC News affiliate KGW8, to address one of the most prevalent myths spread by EV detractors: the one that says EVs can overload the energy grid .
PGE transportation electrification manager Karla Hendrickson shut that nonsense down decisively, touting the electric trucks’ ability to help support the grid during peak load events and calling them out as, “ grid ready assets ,” capable of helping the utility manage periods of high electricity demand while keeping costs low. “Electric school buses are particularly intriguing,” adds said Hendrickson. “Their schedules are predictable and they can spend long stretches parked.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
PGE is already testing the ability to dispatch energy from the state’s deployed fleet of school buses back to the grid.
Big rig, big battery
There are nearly 150,000 registered EVs operating on Oregon roads today, but while the push for electric passenger vehicles gains steam and the electric charging infrastructure to support them is being built out along the state’s travel corridors, the push to electrify medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles is just getting started .
As it gains steam, the push to electrify these vehicles could give the utility access to more stored energy, keeping ratepayers’ bills low, insulating fleets from the wild swings of diesel fuel prices , and (of course) help Oregoons Oregonians breathe a bit easier. Literally.
“These heavy trucks and buses represent a relatively small amount of the fleet of vehicles on the road in Oregon,” explains Gerick Kransky, with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality. “But they represent a disproportionate amount of the emissions that we deal with from transportation.”

source_document.body:
EcoFlow is hoping to make a titanic splash with its new, smaller (but scalable!) residential energy storage lineup that the company is calling a more approachable entry point to its backup battery offerings.
EcoFlow’s new, three-model Titan 5000 range of home backup batteries starts off relatively small with “just” a single, 5 kWh energy storage module that’s enough to keep your refrigerator, lights and Wi-Fi going while keeping your phone and laptop batteries charged. That’s just the start, however, as the system is designed to easily scale up with the addition of more 5,000 Wh modules (hence, the name) to meet your more substantial energy needs — all the way up to 30 kWh.
The company says that’s enough juice to keep an average US home humming along for a full two days without grid power; and that power will (obviis) last a lot longer if you can keep the HVAC system off and keep energy use to a minimum .
Keep it simple
Titan 5000; via EcoFlow.
All three Titan models start with a 5 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) battery and can be expanded to the previously mentioned 30 kWh maximum capacity by stacking more modular batteries, but they differ in output power and capacity for solar panel system integration.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The entry-spec Titan 5000 Classic delivers up to 4 kW of 120V output , while the Titan 5000 steps that up to 7.2 kW continuous power with both 120V and 240V split-phase output available.
The flagship Titan 5000 Plus, meanwhile, also promises 7.2 kW of continuous power, but can reach up to 10 kW of peak power when paired with solar, thanks to EcoFlow’s X-Fusion 2.0 PV Boost technology. The Titan 5000 and Plus can also pair with the EcoFlow Smart Home Panel 10 , which the company claims can help homeowners add backup power without replacing their main electrical panel or enduring a lengthy, complex installation.
“Whole-home backup has traditionally required households to choose between the power they want and the cost and complexity they’re willing to take on,” explains Brian Essenmacher, Head of US Business Development at EcoFlow. “With TITAN, we’re giving more families a practical way to get the power they need , while also helping them manage energy more intelligently every day.”
EcoFlow is allowing “early bird” the chance to lock in one of three bundle deals now with a $50 pre-payment , saving up to $2,999 in November when it officially releases (and when they’ll be expected pay the remaining balance). It’s worth noting, too, that the FCC authorizations for all three of EcoFlow’s new Titan 5000 systems are dated July 20, before the FCC’s July 28 restrictions on foreign-produced inverters kicked in.

2026 Paris Motor Show • 2026 Paris Motor Show: Jeep Reveals Six-Model European Strategy for 2030, Renegade Is Set to Return
This Is Supposedly THE Wildest Lamborghini Revuelto Out There
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke
Have you ever looked at the Lamborghini Revuelto and thought that this thing definitely needs to look more aggressive? Probably not, because it already does. After all, we are talking about the Raging Bull’s new-age flagship supercar, so you know it’s been designed to easily stand out in a sea of exotic rides.
However, regardless of whether you think this model needs to tap into its more aggressive side or not, there are plenty of tuners out there that will gladly take your money in return for all kinds of modifications. The list is comprehensive, as it includes pretty much everything, from various body kits to new wheels, aftermarket suspensions, custom interiors where the sky is basically the limit, and the occasional power boost.
Over the years, because production of the Lamborghini Revuelto started in 2023 at Sant’Agata Bolognese in Italy, we have seen numerous modded examples , some of which were quite fine, and others not so much. We won’t point to any of them in this story, because we are not here to do that. Instead, we will star pointing the spotlight to the pictured example. Or, better said, the one shared on video below at the bottom of the page, and in the gallery above.
The reel was shared on Instagram not long ago by @creativebespoke, which claims that this is the “wildest Revuelto on the planet.” We kid you not, that’s what the short caption, which also includes a few other details about this particular build, says, and while we can definitely think of a few other projects that are on the kitschy side of the tuning game (ahem, Mansory!), this one does not seem to be that controversial.
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke Nevertheless, it is definitely wacky, as this Lamborghini Revuelto features quite a few modifications. These include a widebody kit said to have been signed by Zacoe Performance . And now you know why this supercar looks familiar, don’t you? The front fender and rear three-quarter panel attachments have thus come from the quoted tuner’s portfolio, just like the new front hood, the side skirts, the roof scoop, and a few other things.
The front bumper looks like the OEM piece to us, but it does feature what seems to be a more pronounced apron. Things get even crazier at the rear due to the new diffuser, which four huge extra lights integrated into the fins. These stretch all the from the standard taillights to the lower part of the supercar. And if that wasn’t enough, then you should also know that this machine has an extra brake light in the middle of the diffuser, for a motorsport-like vibe, and a large wing resting on the rear deck.
Creative Bespoke says that the wheels are also on the custom side of things, as if that wasn’t evident from the reel shared below, and these were signed by MV Forged. Unfortunately, we cannot tell you what they’re called, as this information hasn’t been released, nor how big they are. What we can reveal is that the rear ones are a lot wider than the front ones, and they feature a V-spoke pattern. The Balloon White paint protection film will keep the body safe from the usual chips and scratches.
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke Don’t go anywhere yet, because we also have to mention the custom interior. The cockpit’s new upholstery is said to have been handcrafted, and was the work of @cb_autosalon. That’s what @creativebespoke says, anyway, and guess what? We haven’t seen it. That’s because the clip showing this Lamborghini Revuelto does not offer a single glimpse inside the Italian supercar. Thus, we cannot talk about the materials used, the colors, and other work that might have gone into it.
Last but not least, the supercar in question is said to have a “race exhaust system.” Thus, it is definitely more sonorous, though you will not hear it in the clip, because Creative Bespoke chose some background music instead over the V12 burble. We could also be looking at a few extra horses, but the difference is insignificant to alter the supercar’s performance.
Therefore, we will remind you that the Lamborghini Revuelto needs just 2.5 seconds to complete the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) sprint with no outside intervention. It has a top speed of 217 mph (350 kph), and unlocks 1,001 hp (1,015 ps/747 kW) in total from its plug-in hybrid powertrain.
The same electrified 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12 also powers the more track-focused, quicker, rarer, and pricier SuperVeloce. The Lamborghini Revuelto SV premiered earlier this year, boasting 1,050 hp (1,065 ps/783 kW) combined, and needing 2.4 seconds to sprint to 62 mph. The top speed in this case is, however, a bit lower, at 216 mph (348 kph).
Now, if you happened to own a Lamborghini Revuelto and were looking to have it tuned, would you have opted for this makeover? That would be a no for me, because the stock supercar simply looks a lot better in my eyes. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Creative Bespoke International (@creativebespoke)

source_document.body:
U.S. defense firm Anduril could eventually manufacture its newly unveiled Steelfin interceptor missiles in Europe, a company executive said this week, as governments aim to expand air defense production after global conflicts highlighted shortages of interceptor missiles.
“I certainly hope that something like Steelfin could become a capability that we engage with both the Polish customer and industry,” Brian Moran, Anduril’s vice president for Europe, told Reuters on Monday.
“We would definitely consider engaging European partners and customers on this capability.” Steelfin is due to undergo flight testing in 2027, according to Anduril.
Wars in Ukraine and the Gulf have strained stocks of air defense interceptor missiles and caused delivery delays.
Moran said Anduril saw Steelfin as a complementary system that could provide a more affordable interceptor alongside existing missile defense systems like the Patriot and others.
The company is already in talks to establish production in Poland of its Barracuda-500 cruise missile, and Moran said that experience could open the door to additional manufacturing projects.
“We’re having a very good experience with our industry partner here, PGZ,” he said, adding that discussions were also under way with the defense ministry and other government agencies. PGZ is Poland’s state-owned arms group.
Poland, one of NATO’s top defense spenders relative to the size of its economy, is seeking to expand domestic arms production and reduce reliance on foreign suppliers.
Moran said talks with PGZ, its WZL-2 unit and the government were focused on balancing local production with delivery speed and Poland’s specific military requirements.
Asked about growing calls in Europe for defense industrial sovereignty, Moran said the term could mean different things, from security of supply and maintenance capabilities to control over software upgrades and future modifications.
“Sovereignty has a cost. There’s a cost to localization. There’s cost in terms of timing and just schedule. And those need to be considered in light of the threats that Europe collectively is facing.”
While governments also want economic benefits from defense spending, the military outcome is most important, he said, adding that greater localization can come with additional costs and longer timelines.

All-New 2028 Ford F-150 Takes the F-Series to the Fifteenth Generation, Though Only in Fantasy Land
32 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
The winners and losers from America’s September automotive sales charts plus the first nine months of the year already paint a picture of the state of the union across the industry. So, who rules them all?
We’re already well underway with the final three months of the year, and just like it was in every aspect of our modern life, the automotive industry felt like a roller-coaster of emotions. For example, since the entire EV market is suffering in America, it was only logical that General Motors’ luxury arm Cadillac, which has a big EV lineup, would take a massive hit – they dropped 30% during the third quarter and lost 25% of deliveries compared to last year during the nine-month period.
Instead, overall, anyone who makes hybrids was pretty happy with itself, as electrified models that don’t need to be plugged in remained in high demand because gas prices are also extremely high. The small Mazda3 and MX-5 Miata were also bright spots as people increasingly flee back to affordable models due to the incredibly high transaction prices – the average transaction price has reached $50,562, just below the all-time record of $50,614 set in December 2025, according to the latest Kelley Blue Book report from Cox Automotive.
The Ford Mustang , still with no real opponent in the V8 field, was another bright spot, and it might crack 50k sales in 2026 for the first time in the past three years, but the Ford Motor Company is facing massive jeopardy in the truck department next year. That’s because General Motors has come up with a brand-new iteration for both the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 as well as the GMC Sierra 1500, while Ram became the best-selling brand for Stellantis during the third quarter, and the Ram 1500 sales jumped no less than 73 percent as the Hemi V8 is making an awaited comeback.
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube Ram has sold 41% more 1500s this year, as the V8 helped them get back on the right track – the allocation for the new Rumble Bee with the base 5.7-liter sold in less than two hours, and that was the base model, there are two more tiers above it including the 777-hp version akin to the TRX. Clearly, the Ford F-Series needs to up its game in order to keep naming itself the best-selling truck in America and also the most popular nameplate overall.
This year, if they nail the milestone, Ford will claim half a century of continuous laurels as America’s best-selling truck, while overall it would be their 46th. The Blue Oval Company is phasing out important models, like the Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair, and its third quarter sales reflected that: 509,764 vehicles, down 6.6% from last year’s third quarter. The Ford F-Series has been plagued by problems all year long, so Ford is actually lucky that during Q3 they sold 2.4% more, thanks also to the Super Duty, which reached a production of 110,275 trucks, up 4.4% and the best quarterly result in 19 years.
Through September, F-Series sales reached 561,508 trucks, extending the lead over the generation-changing Chevrolet Silverado to more than 140k units. However, GM has two lines, and Silverado plus Sierra continue to outnumber the F-Series. Additionally, the new 1500s are coming to dealerships, and next year they will be brand-new and the F-150 last got the big mid-cycle refresh in late 2023 for the 2024 model year.
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube The Ram 1500 is also going strong thanks to the Hemi V8’s return, and now Stellantis has both off-road performance models – RHO and TRX, as well as a three-model Super Bee family for the road warriors, too. What should Ford do to keep its supremacy? Well, it’s simple, actually: the rumor mill, supported by members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, envisions that it’s time for a new generation, the fifteenth by its F-Series name.
More precisely, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have unofficially imagined the CGI look of the all-new 2028 or 2029 Ford F-150, aka 'XV ', and the channel’s host claims that next year the Ford Motor Company is expected to show us the next generation of their full-sized pickup truck F-150 XV, for the 2028 model year or even the 2029MY.
The host believes that Ford will introduce new EREV (extended range EV) and PHEV (plug-in hybrid) powertrains along with a thoroughly updated P702 architecture. After these thoughts, he passes the baton to the resident virtual artist, who illustrated what the new 2028 or 2029 Ford F-150 fifteenth generation might look like, both inside and outside, as well as complete with a ton of different shades both for the exterior as well as the interior. So, what do you think – yay or nay?

SteelDrop Is One of the Cleanest Retro Teardrop Campers out There – Has a Stainless Steel Exterior
14 photos
Photo: LifeStyle Camper
About four years ago, in 2022, we ran a piece on one of the cleanest and well-executed teardrop campers I've ever seen: the SteelDrop. It’s a teardrop camper that, despite its very American roots, is built by a team over in Ukraine.
When we first encountered the SteelDrop back in 2022, I couldn’t believe my eyes; it’s not American-born, enticing me to dive deeper into the story of this rather under-the-radar camper and its obscure builders, and how glad was I that I did.
Exploring the SteelDrop, I was left in a bit of awe that somewhere in the hidden corners of our world, traditional and very retro camping options still exist, and while the SteelDrop is a camper from over in Ukraine and bound to be a hassle to bring over to the US, the methods and materials that go into the build are simple and inexpensive enough that you may be able to commission one locally in North America.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper Now, the SteelDrop gets its name from nothing more than its outer layer or skin. As you’d expect, steel is used to cover the exterior of the camper, and not fiberglass or any other composite, and clearly not aluminum. The shine is granted by the use of stainless steel, a building block of the industry that we most-often see used in chassis construction and shell frames; some brands build their RVs around steel cages.
But isn’t steel heavy? Well, yes, but clearly, we’re not looking at the thickest sheets in the world, signaled by the way LifeStyle curves this material around the shape of the underlying frame.
Mind you, LifeStyle does create the standard SteelDrop as an unbraked trailer, and this means that its GVWR stands at 750 kg (1,653 lbs). In Europe, that’s the limit to towing a trailer without any special driver’s license classes or categories. In its lightest configuration, the trailer rolls in with a dry weight of just 450 kg (992 lbs), so quite a bit of wiggle room in terms of cargo capacity.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper The use of stainless steel also means a camper that shines in the light from the first few moments of the day when the sun’s rays hit the side in the morning. Heck, you’re bound to also attract countless eyes and onlookers as you roll into a campsite, and you will need one; as a teardrop camper, amenities are limited and often, they are NOT equipped with showers or toilets.
Luckily, you can take the SteelDrop pretty far in terms of upgrades, and annexes are on the menu, side-mounted awnings, the possibility to add an outdoor shower, and even bring a portable toilet along; a shovel should do just fine.
Underneath that layer of steel, LifeStyle uses plywood to craft the shell, a building block of traditional and even modern teardrop campers. Couple this lightweight shell with the aerodynamics provided by the use of a teardrop camper shell, and we have ourselves a camper that may even be suitable for an EV.
Since retro looks and styling are part of the SteelDrop’s attractiveness, LifeStyle does continue to complete the entire habitat in the most traditional ways possible, and that clearly means a rear galley with a lifting hatch to allow for access to your goodies while keeping them free of dust and water, and an interior that is as simple as can be.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper The kitchen is a bit different than others we find in teardrop campers, not in the sense that there are any different features that what we can expect, but the way they’re integrated into the space is what stands apart. Normally, we have slideouts for things like the fridge and cooktop, but LifeStyle chose to integrate everything into the lower half of the kitchen.
In doing so, the fridge stays hidden from sight with a lid that covers it to create a flush countertop, and so does the cooktop and faucet. However, the mounting edges of the systems do stick out a bit and you will need to use a cutting board to level it off for meal prep.
Dry foods will be stored in the cabinet system that’s in place, and at the upper edge of the area is a power bay in case you need some, not to mention a control panel for systems such as pumps, lights, and music.
The latter also tells us that there’s a battery, and depending on the model year and a few other factors, we have 90 Ah to work with and shore power too. The presence of the battery also tells us that we can tap into solar power, but you will need a controller to do so. An inverter is already in place in the SteelDrop.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper Inside the SteelDrop, we have access to a modular mattress (optional) that also allows us to lounge around or sleep too, and we’re also granted access to ample storage for personal belongings. This camper can also include an internal Webasto heater, and we do have control over comfort systems and entertainment inside too.
Take all that, place yourself and your significant other in the middle of it all, and imagine what your mornings would be like with one of these babies parked on a beach somewhere. Just remember that you’ll either need to ship one of these to the US to get your hands on it or, just create your own. There’s sure to be some craftsmen and women in your town that can help you make such a dream a reality.
Back in 2022, when we first covered the SteelDrop , it was selling for around $10,000, but a lot can change in four to five years, and these days, they’re flying off the LifeStyle shelf for around $13,500 in its most standard makeup. This is a price that you receive directly from the production lines, and outside of Ukraine, these babies start at around $20K, or roughly €17,500.
With $20,000, you’re sure to be able to put together a pretty solid “SteelDrop” of your own, because shipping one of these to the US is bound to run you at least $25K, if it’s even cleared for use in NA (North America) by the DOT. Until next time.

Android Auto Users Claim Gemini Is Just Playing a Random Song on Amazon Music
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
Gemini was supposed to provide a significantly upgraded experience on Android Auto, but now that Google Assistant is dead , more and more users discover that this isn’t happening. The latest glitch that seems to be plaguing Android Auto users after the forced transition to Gemini concerns the ability to play a song when requested with a voice command.
More specifically, users discovered that listening to music on Amazon Music is suddenly more difficult after Gemini became the one and only AI-powered assistant on Android Auto.
This is because Gemini seems to ignore users’ voice commands, playing a random song whenever it’s requested to play a specific track. In plain English, Gemini plays whatever song it wants, no matter what tune it’s requested to load.
This only happens in Amazon Music, and users claim that the glitch appeared once Google Assistant was retired.
“Gemini does not work with Amazon Music. I initially went back to using Google Assistant with Android Auto, which played perfectly with Amazon Music,” someone says in a post published in early October on Google’s forums .
“However, Gemini has now been forced upon us. I understand (from asking Gemini!) that Google needs to create an app extension for Amazon Music to resolve this (and that Google Assistant worked differently and didn't require one), but apparently there is no timescale for when / if this might happen.”
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Several others joined the conversation, and as it turns out, this is what more users are experiencing on Android Auto after the transition from Google Assistant to Gemini. Everybody is reporting the same glitch, with Gemini just playing a random song instead of the track it’s requested to load in Amazon Music.
Oddly, not everybody is affected.
I just tried asking Gemini to play Metallica - Nothing Else Matters on Amazon Music, and the AI assistant followed the instructions correctly. Random songs don’t seem to be played in my car, so it’s clear that not everybody is affected. I use Android Auto 18.0 with a Google Pixel 10 Pro XL.
Interestingly, someone with the same phone says they do see the bug.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution “Using [the app] on my Android Auto device voice control to play a specific song, the song is first confirmed by Gemini, but then a casual song is played. I have an Amazon Music Unlimited subscription. I have a Pixel 10. All devices and Apps are up to date,” one user explains.
While Gemini failing to run a simple task isn’t necessarily surprising, especially considering the bugs the new AI-powered assistant has struggled with lately, users complain that Google Assistant worked correctly before it was discontinued.
Several users explained on the forums that this is precisely the reason why they went back from Gemini to Google Assistant when this option was still available. They downgraded because Gemini couldn’t play Amazon Music songs correctly, and going back to Google Assistant temporarily was seen by everybody as a way to continue to use the music streaming service until Google comes up with a patch.
Google doesn’t appear to have addressed the glitch, and now that going back to Google Assistant is no longer an option, users are being forced to look for other solutions.
“I am also suffering from the same issue. When Gemini was initially pushed on my device around 5 months ago I switched back to assistant and provided this reason (lack of voice control for Amazon music when using Android Auto) as the reason. Now Gemini has been forced up on us, and Amazon Music still doesn't work. Very poor from Google,” someone explains.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The problem is that no workaround has been found for this glitch. The typical Android Auto fixes don’t seem to correct the error, as clearing the cache, reinstalling and updating Android Auto, and everything else that might resolve an Android Auto issue don’t make a difference. This means that a patch from Google is the only way to continue to use Amazon Music with Gemini, so without it, users are forced to just avoid voice commands entirely.
A Google Community Specialist replied on October 7 and revealed that additional information about the glitch is necessary. Users who reported the problem were contacted by email to provide more data, so right now, it’s unclear if the investigation has made any progress.
Meanwhile, keeping automatic app updates enabled is highly recommended for users battling this error. Once Google releases a fix, you should get it as an automatic update, though it’s unclear when this is supposed to happen. Android Auto 18.0 has just started rolling out, but it doesn’t seem to include a fix - let me know in the comments box below if this new version corrected the Gemini and Amazon Music problem for you.
Google hasn’t offered additional data, so share your experience with Gemini and Amazon Music in the comments box below if you want to help the search giant come up with a fix faster.

2028 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Is the Monster Rival SUVs Have Bad Dreams About
63 photos
Photo: Mercedes-AMG
As a sort of general, unspoken rule, carmakers don’t usually come out with information, details, and photos of new car models over the weekend. Yet, this Saturday, that’s exactly what German carmaker Mercedes-AMG did, as it pulled the wraps off the second vehicle it built on the AMG.EA architecture.
Following in the footsteps of the AMG GT 4‑Door Coupe, the newcomer is called the 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV, and it makes no secret of what it is all about: a full-size SUV powered by an electric drivetrain, meant to offer, in the same package, the performance levels usually associated with AMG and the practicality of a vehicle in this class.
The GT is not just any other SUV, but the first one to have been specifically developed from the ground up in-house by the high-performance brand. It’s also the first Mercedes to come with the AMG Active Ride Control+ system that throws into the mix active pitch and roll stabilization to contribute to a smoother ride.
We’ve already covered the basics of what the newcomer family brings to the world of performance SUVs, and we’ll go through that again later in the story. Until then, though, I think it’s worth having a look at the model that’ll spearhead the range, the AMG GT 63 SUV.
This model is the most potent of the lineup of three SUV versions that will be sold as part of this family, at least as it shapes up to be for now – the other two being the entry-level Mercedes‑AMG GT 53 SUV and the Mercedes‑AMG GT 55 SUV.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG As specced for the American market, the 63 is, just like its siblings, built on a 119.7-inch wheelbase and measures a little over 200 inches long, almost 80 inches wide, and a tad over 65 inches tall. Despite these dimensions and its rather bulky appearance, it comes with a drag coefficient of 0.27, which is about the same as the Hyundai Ioniq 9 and the Toyota Prius.
That matters, as the easier this thing cuts through the air that opposes its forward motion, the more drivers can squeeze out of its electric powertrain. And the numbers provided by Mercedes are impressive even on paper.
The AMG GT 63 SUV is animated by a trio of axial flux motors that deliver a peak output of 1,153 hp and 1,475 lb-ft of torque. When it comes to continuous output, though, horsepower levels drop to 711.
That’s still enough to get the beast, which tips the scales at 5,941 pounds (2,695 kg, curb weight), to an electronically limited top speed of 168 mph (270 kph), and allows it to accelerate from zero to 60 mph in just 2.6 seconds.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG The three electric motors are only one of the two major components the SUV relies on to become a nightmare for the competition. The other one is the battery pack, a 128-kWh Formula 1-based 800-volt piece of hardware with directly cooled cylindrical cells, which is good for a maximum range of 435 miles (700 km, as measured under WLTP).
The pack supports a 710-kW DC charging capacity, and that translates into 280 miles (450 km) of range being gained in just ten minutes of being plugged in. That also means the state of charge can get from ten to 80 percent in just 12 minutes.
The 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 packs all the latest technologies developed by Mercedes-AMG, including an Aerokinetics roof spoiler and air panel designed to reduce aerodynamic drag, and a number of seven drive programs, including one that replicates the sound of a V8 engine for those who might miss such a thing,
Mercedes will release the AMG GT 63 SUV onto the American market in the summer of next year, and that means pricing for it hasn’t been announced yet. The same happens for the two other models in the range.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG As a reminder, the mid-range AMG GT 55 SUV is equipped with the same electric powertrain as the 63, but offers lower numbers in terms of performance: 805 peak horsepower (711 hp continuous) and 1,372 lb-ft of torque. Because it uses the same battery pack as its higher-spec sibling, range stays the same.
The entry-level AMG GT 53 SUV relies on a completely different powertrain, consisting of a 106-kWh battery and two permanently excited synchronous electric motors. The motors crank out a combined 536 hp peak and 362 hp continuous, while maximum range stands at 415 miles (668 km).
The 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 will not have it easy going up against the likes of the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric or the Lucid Air Gravity GT-S, but neither will these rival electric SUVs. The arrival of the new AMG beast is likely to energize the market in the coming years as the battle for supremacy in this segment heats up.
We’ll keep an eye on AMG and report back when pricing for these three newcomers is announced. Until then, one more thing: Mercedes will offer no less than 60 exclusive Manufaktur colors for the SUV, along with AMG wheels that can be enhanced with new color accents for the first time.
